name: FlashInfer: a kernel-selection layer over FlashAttention, cuDNN, CUTLASS and TensorRT-LLM
arithmetic_intensity: FlashInfer is not itself an arithmetic mechanism; it is the layer where backend choice decides which arithmetic is done. Recorded as custom_kernel because the engine-level effect is a discrete change in the kernels executing the same math. Its kernels change the bytes/FLOPs trade by adding: paged and ragged KV-cache layouts (so decode reads a gathered block table instead of a dense cache - same FLOPs, different access pattern and potentially more uncoalesced reads), cascade attention (a hierarchical pass that reads a shared prefix KV once and reuses it across requests rather than per-request, which cuts HBM bytes for shared prefixes), POD-attention (fused prefill+decode for a mixed batch, saving a kernel boundary and the re-read of the shared prefix), block-sparse and variable block-sparse plans, and FP8/FP4 GEMM and MoE paths (per-tensor, groupwise, NVFP4 and MXFP4 block-scaled) which do change the FLOP cost by doubling or quadrupling tensor-core throughput.
scales_with: batch_size (decode vs prefill vs mixed-batch kernel selection)
workarounds: Backend selection by compute capability: README lists support from SM75 (Turing) through SM90 (Hopper), SM100/SM103 (Blackwell), SM110 (Jetson Thor) and SM120/SM121 (RTX 50, DGX Spark) - and warns 'Not all features are supported across all compute capabilities'
Sorting-free top-k / top-p / min-p sampling to remove a sort from the sampling path
Pre-compiled cubin wheels (flashinfer-cubin) plus a JIT cache so per-arch kernel selection does not become a cold-start compile
Low-latency and high-throughput variants of the same op, chosen by workload
notes: There is already an engine record for FlashInfer (engines/flashinfer presumably) - this flop record deliberately records the kernels rather than duplicating the engine. The decision-relevant fact: because FlashInfer wraps other people's kernels, a benchmark on 'FlashInfer' is a benchmark on whichever backend it selected for that arch, and that differs per GPU. Features that are CUDA-only versus features that need a specific arch are not the same list. Sampling note: the sorting-free sampler is documented in a 2025-03-10 FlashInfer blog. Verified against the repo README only; no performance number is taken from here.
